answer: The walnut shells stay sealed until payout, when a zephyr sweeps them open and each shell spills its pigment. Every identity presses one pigment sample into a walnut shell at registration, backed by a 600,000 POA stake. Two shells spilling the same pigment belong to one operator: both rewards burn, both stakes pass to honest peers, and the operator pays a 550,000 POA fine per fake. One fake costs 1,150,000 POA, and four fakes cost 4,600,000 POA before any payout clears.
